title: Neighbor-Consistent Neural Filters for Robust Personal Sound Zones Under Localization Uncertainty
summary: Coordinate-conditioned neural networks can generate head-tracked personal sound zone (PSZ) loudspeaker filters in real time, but they are sensitive to localization uncertainty. Small fluctuations in estimated listener coordinates, caused by optical distortion, temporary occlusions, or tracking jitter, may produce large filter changes even when listeners are physically stationary. This paper proposes neighbor-consistent neural filters that regularize the coordinate-to-filter mapping by penalizing filter differences at randomly perturbed neighboring coordinates during training. To evaluate robustness against tracking noise, we introduce a decoupled protocol that fixes the acoustic transfer functions at a physical anchor while perturbing only the coordinate inputs used for filter generation. Isolation quality and local stability are evaluated using neighborhood median and lower-tail statistics of inter-zone and inter-program isolation, together with spatial variation rates that quantify metric sensitivity within a coordinate neighborhood. In simulation with a split-band woofer-tweeter system and 25 randomly sampled anchor positions, neighbor consistency reduces the root-mean-square (RMS) variation rate by up to 55.9% in the woofer band and 30.3% in the tweeter band while largely preserving isolation quality and improving lower-tail robustness. In in-situ measurements using a 24-driver array and two stationary head-and-torso simulators, the proposed regularization improves worst-case neighborhood isolation by up to 16.9% and reduces spatial variation rates by up to 61.8%. These results demonstrate that neighbor-consistency regularization effectively stabilizes PSZ rendering under localization uncertainty.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes neighbor-consistent neural filters that regularize coordinate-to-filter mapping by penalizing filter differences at randomly perturbed neighboring coordinates during training, reducing filter sensitivity to localization uncertainty in head-tracked personal sound zone systems. The method achieves up to 61.8% reduction in spatial variation rates and up to 16.9% improvement in worst-case isolation in real measurements, while largely preserving isolation quality.
AI.motivation: Coordinate-conditioned neural networks for PSZ loudspeaker filters are sensitive to localization uncertainty—small fluctuations in estimated listener coordinates (due to optical distortion, occlusions, or tracking jitter) cause large filter changes even when listeners are physically stationary.
AI.method: Neighbor-consistent neural filters that penalize filter differences at randomly perturbed neighboring coordinates during training; a decoupled evaluation protocol that fixes acoustic transfer functions at a physical anchor while perturbing only coordinate inputs; evaluation using neighborhood median/lower-tail statistics and spatial variation rates.
AI.result: Simulation: RMS variation rate reduced by 55.9% (woofer band) and 30.3% (tweeter band). In-situ: worst-case neighborhood isolation improved by 16.9%, spatial variation rates reduced by 61.8%.
AI.conclusion: Neighbor-consistency regularization effectively stabilizes PSZ rendering under localization uncertainty, preserving isolation quality while significantly improving robustness.

title: Effective User-defined Keyword Spotting with Dual-stage Matching, Multi-modal Enrollment, and Continual Adaptation
comment: 14 pages, 13 figures, 12 tables. Accepted by TASLP
summary: User-defined keyword spotting (KWS) is crucial for personalized voice interaction, yet existing methods face several challenges: (1) insufficient discriminability among confusable words, (2) performance inconsistency across speakers with varying pronunciations, and (3) high data cost to ensure reliable wake-word performance. In this paper, we introduce DMA-KWS, an efficient and robust framework for user-defined keyword spotting. First, it adopts a dual-stage matching pipeline: CTC decoding with streaming phoneme search to locate candidate segments, followed by QbyT with a phoneme matcher for fine-grained verification, enabling it to better distinguish confusable words. Next, multi-modal enrollment fuses user-specific speech with text embeddings to further improve accuracy for registered users. Finally, a parameter-efficient continual adaptation mechanism performs lightweight updates using synthetic and real data. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of DMA-KWS. On the LibriPhrase Hard subset, it achieves 97.85% AUC and 6.13% EER, reaching state-of-the-art performance. In speaker-dependent settings, DMA-KWS consistently outperforms text-only enrollment, demonstrating significant performance gains. Moreover, the proposed parameter-efficient fine-tuning mechanism adapts DMA-KWS with only 187k updated parameters, further enhancing KWS performance while ensuring suitability for on-device deployment.

AI.tldr: DMA-KWS is a dual-stage matching framework for user-defined keyword spotting that uses CTC decoding with streaming phoneme search and QbyT verification, multi-modal enrollment, and parameter-efficient continual adaptation, achieving state-of-the-art 97.85% AUC and 6.13% EER on LibriPhrase Hard with only 187k updated parameters.
AI.motivation: Existing user-defined KWS methods suffer from insufficient discriminability among confusable words, performance inconsistency across speakers with varying pronunciations, and high data cost for reliable wake-word performance.
AI.method: DMA-KWS employs (1) dual-stage matching: CTC decoding with streaming phoneme search for candidate segment localization, followed by QbyT with a phoneme matcher for fine-grained verification; (2) multi-modal enrollment fusing user-specific speech and text embeddings; (3) parameter-efficient continual adaptation using synthetic and real data with only 187k updated parameters.
AI.result: On LibriPhrase Hard: 97.85% AUC and 6.13% EER (SOTA). In speaker-dependent settings, multi-modal enrollment outperforms text-only enrollment. Adaptation uses only 187k parameters, suitable for on-device deployment.
AI.conclusion: DMA-KWS effectively addresses confusable word discrimination, speaker variance, and data cost challenges, achieving robust and efficient user-defined KWS suitable for on-device deployment.

title: RobustSpeechFlow: Learning Robust Text-to-Speech Trajectories via Augmentation-based Contrastive Flow Matching
summary: While flow-matching text-to-speech (TTS) achieves strong zero-shot speaker similarity and naturalness, it remains susceptible to content fidelity issues, particularly skip and repeat errors from imperfect alignment. We propose RobustSpeechFlow, a training strategy that improves alignment robustness by extending contrastive flow matching with length-preserving repeat and skip latent augmentations. Requiring no external aligners or preference data, our method directly penalizes realistic failure modes and readily integrates into existing pipelines. On Seed-TTS-eval, it reduces the word error rate (WER) from 1.44 to 1.38 using only 0.06B parameters. On our ZERO500 benchmark, it delivers consistent intelligibility improvements across diverse speaker and prosody conditions; at NFE=24, it reduces English character error rate (CER) from 0.48\% to 0.35\% and Korean CER from 0.81\% to 0.57\%. Audio samples: https://robustspeechflow.github.io/

AI.tldr: RobustSpeechFlow improves the alignment robustness of flow-matching TTS by extending contrastive flow matching with length-preserving repeat and skip latent augmentations, reducing word/character error rates on multiple benchmarks without needing external aligners or preference data.
AI.motivation: Flow-matching TTS suffers from content fidelity issues (skip and repeat errors) due to imperfect alignment, which degrades speech intelligibility.
AI.method: A training strategy that extends contrastive flow matching with length-preserving repeat and skip latent augmentations, directly penalizing realistic failure modes without external aligners or preference data.
AI.result: Seed-TTS-eval: WER reduced from 1.44 to 1.38 (0.06B params). ZERO500 benchmark: English CER reduced from 0.48% to 0.35%; Korean CER from 0.81% to 0.57% (NFE=24).
AI.conclusion: RobustSpeechFlow effectively improves alignment robustness and intelligibility across diverse speaker and prosody conditions, integrating readily into existing TTS pipelines.

title: Automatic Contextual Audio Denoising
summary: Audio context determines which sound components and sources are relevant and which can be perceived as irrelevant (noise) by listeners. For example, traffic noise is informative in urban surveillance but noise for a phone call at the same location. Most current audio denoising systems apply fixed target-noise definitions, often removing useful components in one context while failing to suppress irrelevant components. To address this, we introduce the concept automatic contextual audio denoising (ACAD) which defines target and noise based on the inferred context. In this work, we restrict context to be associated with an acoustic scene class. We label sound events outside the event distribution of a scene class (noise) as out-of-context (OC) and events typical for that scene as in-context (IC). We implement a deep learning method that automatically infers the context of the audio signal and removes OC components, and benchmark it against variants: without context inference, with oracle context, and with separately provided uninformative context. On paired clean/noisy data across diverse contexts, where OC components in one context may be IC in another, our proposed method outperforms other approaches across standard objective metrics, indicating that the model can infer context and context-dependent processing can enhance denoising.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Automatic Contextual Audio Denoising (ACAD), which uses inferred acoustic scene context to distinguish between in-context (relevant) and out-of-context (noise) sound events, and implements a deep learning method that outperforms fixed approaches on diverse noisy data.
AI.motivation: Current audio denoising systems apply fixed target-noise definitions, which are context-insensitive—they may remove useful components in one context while failing to suppress irrelevant components in another, limiting their effectiveness across varying acoustic environments.
AI.method: The authors introduce ACAD, which defines target and noise based on inferred acoustic scene context. They label sound events outside a scene's event distribution as out-of-context (noise) and typical events as in-context. A deep learning model automatically infers audio context and removes out-of-context components.
AI.result: On paired clean/noisy data across diverse contexts (where out-of-context components in one context may be in-context in another), the proposed method outperforms baselines (without context inference, with oracle context, and with uninformative context) across standard objective metrics.
AI.conclusion: The model can effectively infer context, and context-dependent processing enhances denoising performance compared to fixed approaches.

title: Academic Text-to-Music Grand Challenge: Datasets, Baselines, and Evaluation Methods
comment: Accepted to IEEE ICME 2026 Grand Challenge Paper
summary: This paper presents an overview and the technical framework of the ICME 2026 Grand Challenge on Academic Text-to-Music Generation (ATTM). Despite the rapid progress in text-to-music generation (TTM) systems, the field is currently dominated by models trained on massive proprietary datasets with industrial-scale computational resources, creating a significant barrier for academic research. To address this, the ATTM Challenge establishes a fair-play benchmark that requires participants to train generative models strictly from scratch using a standardized, CC-licensed subset of the MTG-Jamendo dataset containing only instrumental music. The challenge is divided into two tracks: the Efficiency Track (limited to 500M parameters) and the Performance Track (no parameter limit). Submissions are evaluated through a multi-stage process involving objective metrics, including Frechet Audio Distance, CLAP score, and a novel Concept Coverage Score (CCS), followed by a subjective listening test. By providing open-source baselines, preprocessing pipelines, reference captions, and public evaluation code for computing FAD and CLAP, this challenge aims to facilitate and promote TTM research in academic contexts.

AI.tldr: The ICME 2026 Grand Challenge on Academic Text-to-Music Generation (ATTM) establishes a fair-play benchmark requiring participants to train models from scratch on a standardized CC-licensed instrumental subset of MTG-Jamendo, with two tracks (Efficiency ≤500M params, Performance unlimited), evaluated via objective metrics (FAD, CLAP, novel CCS) and subjective listening tests, aiming to democratize TTM research in academia.
AI.motivation: Current text-to-music generation is dominated by models trained on massive proprietary datasets with industrial-scale compute, creating barriers for academic research. This challenge aims to lower these barriers by providing standardized open resources.
AI.method: Participants train generative models from scratch on a CC-licensed instrumental subset of MTG-Jamendo. Two tracks: Efficiency Track (≤500M parameters) and Performance Track (unlimited). Evaluation uses objective metrics (FAD, CLAP score, and a novel Concept Coverage Score) plus subjective listening tests. Open-source baselines, preprocessing pipelines, reference captions, and public evaluation code are provided.
AI.result: Establishes a standardized benchmark with two tracks, multi-stage evaluation combining objective metrics and subjective listening, and provides open-source infrastructure to facilitate academic TTM research.
AI.conclusion: The ATTM Grand Challenge promotes and facilitates text-to-music research in academic contexts by providing a fair, reproducible benchmark with open resources, reducing the dependency on proprietary datasets and large-scale compute.

title: Resilient Energy-Based Control for DC Data Centers under Grid and Load Disturbances
summary: This paper presents a passivity-based control framework for AC-DC converters supplying non-passive Information Technology rack loads in DC data centers. Unlike conventional cascaded proportional-integral controllers that ensure stability only near nominal operating points, the proposed method is derived from the system total energy balance using the Port-Hamiltonian formulation. By shaping the stored energy and injecting virtual damping through a lossless interconnection with a PH controller, the converter behaves as a passive system even when interfaced with non-passive loads or under grid disturbances. The closed-loop system guarantees asymptotic voltage regulation and strict energy dissipation without assuming constant grid voltage or frequency. Simulation studies under realistic load and fault scenarios validate that the proposed controller achieves smaller voltage deviations, faster recovery, and superior robustness, demonstrating its suitability for future high-efficiency DC data-center architectures.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a passivity-based control framework using Port-Hamiltonian formulation for AC-DC converters in DC data centers, ensuring asymptotic voltage regulation and strict energy dissipation even with non-passive IT loads and grid disturbances, validated through simulations showing superior performance over conventional PI controllers.
AI.motivation: Conventional cascaded proportional-integral (PI) controllers for AC-DC converters in DC data centers only ensure stability near nominal operating points and cannot guarantee stability when interfaced with non-passive Information Technology rack loads or under grid disturbances.
AI.method: The control framework is derived from the system total energy balance using the Port-Hamiltonian (PH) formulation, shaping stored energy and injecting virtual damping through a lossless interconnection with a PH controller to make the converter behave passively.
AI.result: Simulation studies under realistic load and fault scenarios demonstrate smaller voltage deviations, faster recovery, and superior robustness compared to conventional cascaded PI controllers.
AI.conclusion: The proposed passivity-based controller is suitable for future high-efficiency DC data-center architectures, guaranteeing asymptotic voltage regulation and strict energy dissipation without assuming constant grid voltage or frequency.

title: Real-time, EDM-inspired sonfication of the activity of a supercomputer
summary: The project described in this paper explores the informative sonification of data received in real time from a supercomputer. These data capture the current activities in all the nodes of the computer, therefore, their sonification functions as a form of continuous monitoring of the nodes' behavior and, by extension, of the system as a whole. Because such monitoring is theoretically unending, the resulting sonification must be musically capable of conveying information through sound in a way that remains both intelligible and engaging over long durations. Rather than imposing a predefined musical style onto the data, we sought to identify one which the data themselves could plausibly support. From a small set of candidates, we selected EDM because it is a family of genres whose structural and temporal characteristics align well with continuous, data-driven processes and long-term listening. Through this style-based approach, this research builds on the long tradition of computer data sonification while uniquely combining three elements rarely addressed together: monitoring (rather than debugging) as the primary goal, real-time (rather than post-mortem) data interpretation, and generation of virtually infinite and stylistically coherent (rather than incongruous) music.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a real-time sonification system that monitors supercomputer node activities by generating continuous, stylistically coherent EDM music from live data, combining monitoring, real-time interpretation, and infinite musical generation.
AI.motivation: To create a sonification system capable of monitoring supercomputer node behavior continuously through sound, while maintaining both intelligibility and engagement over theoretically unending durations.
AI.method: The authors sonify real-time data from supercomputer nodes using Electronic Dance Music (EDM) as the musical style, selected because its structural and temporal characteristics align with continuous, data-driven processes. Rather than imposing a predefined style, they identified EDM as a style the data could plausibly support from a set of candidates.
AI.result: A system that generates virtually infinite, stylistically coherent music for continuous monitoring of supercomputer node activities, combining three rarely addressed elements: monitoring as the primary goal, real-time data interpretation, and generation of infinite coherent music.
AI.conclusion: The style-based EDM sonification approach successfully enables long-duration, intelligible, and engaging monitoring of supercomputer systems, building on the tradition of computer data sonification with a unique combination of monitoring, real-time processing, and stylistic coherence.

title: Disturbance Rejection Control under Nested Signal Temporal Logic Specifications: A Recursive Design Approach
summary: This paper investigates the control synthesis for continuous-time uncertain systems under nested Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications containing nested temporal operators. Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) are utilized herein to encode STL formulas into system constraints. However, traditional CBF designs fail to encode nested STL formulas, whereas recent reachability analysis-based methods capable of handling such formulas are inapplicable to uncertain systems and suffer from a severe computational burden. To overcome these challenges, a novel recursive CBF design procedure based on a modified STL tree (sTLT) is proposed to yield explicit parameterized CBFs. Within this framework, sliding window variables are introduced to capture complex temporal relationships. Crucially, satisfying the resulting CBF constraints is proven to guarantee the fulfillment of the STL specifications. To render the proposed recursive CBF design applicable to systems subject to uncertain disturbance, a novel controller based on reconstructed CBF using quadratic programming (QP) is proposed, ensuring strict CBF constraint satisfaction under disturbances. In contrast to existing methods, the proposed reconstructed CBF approach requires no prior knowledge of the disturbances while relaxing initial safety assumptions. Simulation results validate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

AI.tldr: A recursive Control Barrier Function (CBF) design using modified STL trees (sTLT) and sliding window variables is proposed to handle nested Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications for continuous-time uncertain systems, with a reconstructed CBF-based QP controller ensuring constraint satisfaction under unknown disturbances.
AI.motivation: Existing CBF designs cannot encode nested STL formulas, while reachability-based methods that can handle such formulas are not applicable to uncertain systems and suffer from high computational burden.
AI.method: Proposes a recursive CBF design procedure based on a modified STL tree (sTLT) with sliding window variables to capture complex temporal relationships, plus a reconstructed CBF-based quadratic programming controller that ensures strict constraint satisfaction under disturbances without prior knowledge of disturbances.
AI.result: Simulation results validate the efficacy of the proposed approach; the method guarantees STL specification satisfaction via CBF constraints and handles uncertain systems without requiring prior disturbance knowledge.
AI.conclusion: The proposed recursive CBF design with sTLT and reconstructed CBF-QP controller successfully overcomes limitations of traditional CBF and reachability methods for nested STL specifications under uncertainty, with relaxed initial safety assumptions.

title: Secure Coordination for Vertiport Sequencing in Advanced Air Mobility
summary: Advanced air mobility operations will require reliable coordination mechanisms for managing dense traffic near vertiports. However, sequencing decisions may become vulnerable when they rely on potentially falsified self-reported information such as estimated time of arrival. Self-interested vehicles may misreport their arrival times to obtain favorable landing priority, while malicious actors may spoof information to disrupt sequencing decisions or induce unnecessary congestion. This paper studies secure coordination for vertiport sequencing under sensing uncertainty. We consider a coordinator that combines self-reported Remote-ID information with externally obtained surveillance measurements to check reports and assign separation-feasible arrival schedules. Since surveillance-based estimates are uncertain, falsified reports may remain consistent with the sensing uncertainty region and cannot always be rejected outright. We therefore formulate sequencing as a robust design problem over this uncertainty region. Self-interested misreporting is modeled as a strategic deviation that improves the reporting vehicle's own sequencing outcome, whereas malicious spoofing is modeled as an adversarial disturbance that degrades the system-level objective. The final paper will develop robust sequencing rules over surveillance-consistent uncertainty sets and evaluate their performance in representative vertiport sequencing scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper studies secure vertiport sequencing under sensing uncertainty, where a coordinator combines self-reported Remote-ID data with surveillance measurements to detect falsified information. It formulates sequencing as a robust design problem over uncertainty regions, modeling self-interested misreporting as strategic deviation and malicious spoofing as adversarial disturbance.
AI.motivation: Sequencing decisions for vertiport operations may be vulnerable when relying on potentially falsified self-reported information (e.g., estimated time of arrival). Self-interested vehicles may misreport for favorable landing priority, while malicious actors may spoof information to disrupt sequencing or induce congestion.
AI.method: The coordinator combines self-reported Remote-ID information with externally obtained surveillance measurements to check reports. Sequencing is formulated as a robust design problem over the sensing uncertainty region. Self-interested misreporting is modeled as strategic deviation (improving reporting vehicle's outcome) while malicious spoofing is modeled as adversarial disturbance (degrading system-level objective).
AI.result: The paper develops robust sequencing rules over surveillance-consistent uncertainty sets and evaluates their performance in representative vertiport sequencing scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Secure coordination for vertiport sequencing is achievable through robust design that accounts for sensing uncertainty, enabling detection of falsified reports even when they fall within surveillance-consistent uncertainty regions.

title: Live Music Diffusion Models: Efficient Fine-Tuning and Post-Training of Interactive Diffusion Music Generators
summary: Interactive streaming music generation promises the use of generative models for live performance and co-creation that is impossible with offline models. However, SOTA models exist in the discrete-AR regime, requiring industrial levels of compute for both training and inference. In this work, we investigate whether audio diffusion models, with their wide support in the open-source community but non-streaming bidirectional nature, can be repurposed efficiently into interactive models accessible on consumer hardware. By taking a critical look at the modern pipeline for block-wise outpainting diffusion, we identify critical inefficiencies during inference that result in strictly worse computational efficiency than their discrete-AR counterparts. We propose Live Music Diffusion Models (LMDMs), a simple modification of the generative diffusion process that recovers, and then outperforms, the inference complexity of the discrete Live Music Models (LMMs) through block-wise KV Caching. Unlike LMMs, LMDMs further enable stable post-training alignment through our novel ARC-Forcing paradigm, reducing error accumulation without any explicit RL or reward models. We demonstrate the application of LMDMs in a number of creative domains, including text-conditioned generation, sketch-based music synthesis, and jamming. We finally show how LMDMs can be used as a generative instrument in a real artist-AI collaboration, utilizing LMDMs as a "generative delay" to transform musicians' improvisation live for variable timbral effects while running locally on a consumer gaming laptop.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Live Music Diffusion Models (LMDMs), which modify the diffusion process to make interactive streaming music generation efficient on consumer hardware by using block-wise KV caching, achieving better inference complexity than discrete autoregressive models and enabling stable post-training alignment through ARC-Forcing.
AI.motivation: Interactive streaming music generation is promising for live performance and co-creation, but state-of-the-art discrete autoregressive models require industrial-level compute. The authors investigate whether audio diffusion models (which are more accessible via open-source but inherently non-streaming and bidirectional) can be efficiently repurposed for interactive use on consumer hardware.
AI.method: The paper identifies critical inefficiencies in block-wise outpainting diffusion pipelines. LMDMs introduce a simple modification to the generative diffusion process with block-wise KV caching to recover and surpass the inference complexity of discrete Live Music Models (LMMs). Additionally, ARC-Forcing is proposed for stable post-training alignment without reinforcement learning or reward models.
AI.result: LMDMs outperform discrete LMMs in inference complexity, enable stable post-training alignment via ARC-Forcing, and are demonstrated across text-conditioned generation, sketch-based music synthesis, and jamming. The model runs locally on a consumer gaming laptop as a "generative delay" effect for real-time artist-AI collaboration.
AI.conclusion: LMDMs successfully repurpose non-streaming diffusion models into interactive music generation systems that are efficient on consumer hardware, opening up new creative possibilities for live performance and co-creation without requiring industrial-scale compute.

title: System Level Analysis and Management of Orbital Debris Using Empirical Dynamic Modeling
comment: 23 pages, 9 figures, Journal of Aerospace Information Systems (accepted)
summary: Orbital debris is a pressing problem which presents a danger to global space operations and a barrier to continued development of the space economy and space infrastructure. As research continues regarding orbital debris, there is a need for tools to understand the system-level implications of orbital debris solutions. This research considers the orbital debris problem as a dynamic process. Based on dynamic system theories, time-series variables of the numbers of orbital debris, orbital objects, and object launches should be causally linked, which means they share a common system attractor manifold. We propose a data-driven method based on complexity science to reconstruct a shadow attractor of the dynamic system using limited observable variables. The reconstructed shadow attractor helps us to understand the fundamental system dynamics for orbital debris and enables us to simulate the future of the orbital debris system based on changes to policy. These findings represent a significant advancement in our ability to understand high level impacts of space system policy with limited data available.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a data-driven method based on complexity science and dynamic systems theory to reconstruct a shadow attractor of the orbital debris system using limited observable variables, enabling simulation of future debris scenarios and policy impact analysis.
AI.motivation: Orbital debris poses a danger to space operations and infrastructure development; there is a need for tools to understand system-level implications of debris solutions.
AI.method: Treats orbital debris as a dynamic process where time-series variables (debris counts, orbital objects, launches) are causally linked via a common system attractor manifold. Uses complexity science to reconstruct a shadow attractor from limited observable variables.
AI.result: The reconstructed shadow attractor reveals fundamental system dynamics and enables simulation of future debris system states under different policy changes.
AI.conclusion: This advancement improves our ability to understand high-level impacts of space system policy despite limited data availability.

title: AdaPTwin: Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Predictive Digital Twin for Proactive Radio Resource Management in Vehicular Networks
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: The highly dynamic nature of vehicular networks necessitates proactive and site-specific radio resource management (RRM) to achieve ultra-reliable low-latency communications. While Network Digital Twins (NDTs) have emerged as a promising enabler, ray-tracing remains time-consuming, challenging accurate RRM under latency constraints. We propose AdaPTwin, an adaptive multi-fidelity predictive NDT for proactive and latency-aware RRM in vehicular networks. Unlike single- and multi-fidelity NDTs with fixed fidelity levels, AdaPTwin dynamically adjusts NDT fidelity based on network conditions. The framework adopts a hierarchical cloud-edge architecture, where computationally intensive fidelity selection is performed periodically in the cloud, and the proactive RRM loop operates in real-time at the edge. The edge-based proactive RRM task consists of channel prediction between vehicles and roadside units (RSUs) via trajectory forecasting and look-ahead ray tracing, followed by RRM execution. A transformer model enhanced with continual and transfer learning enables vehicular trajectory prediction while adapting to new environments and traffic patterns. Ray-tracing is performed using NVIDIA Sionna by exploiting a dynamically updated virtual environment to ensure realistic radio propagation within the NDT. Furthermore, a joint RSU beamforming and vehicle-RSU association problem is formulated to maximize proportionally fair sum-rate, and it is efficiently solved using a scalable multi-start iterative coordinate descent algorithm. Comparisons against reactive, single-fidelity, and non-adaptive predictive NDTs under realistic vehicular conditions confirm that AdaPTwin successfully adapts to diverse scenarios where other frameworks fail. Ultimately, AdaPTwin achieves up to 90% sum-rate gain and 80% outage probability reduction compared to non-adaptive NDTs, while maintaining real-time performance.

AI.tldr: AdaPTwin is an adaptive multi-fidelity predictive Network Digital Twin (NDT) framework for proactive radio resource management (RRM) in vehicular networks. It dynamically adjusts NDT fidelity based on network conditions using a hierarchical cloud-edge architecture, combining trajectory prediction (via continual/transfer learning-enhanced transformers), look-ahead ray tracing (NVIDIA Sionna), and a scalable multi-start iterative coordinate descent algorithm for joint RSU beamforming and vehicle-RSU association. Compared to non-adaptive NDTs, AdaPTwin achieves up to 90% sum-rate gain and 80% outage probability reduction while maintaining real-time performance.
AI.motivation: Vehicular networks are highly dynamic and require proactive, site-specific RRM for ultra-reliable low-latency communications. Existing NDTs using ray-tracing are too time-consuming for latency-constrained RRM, and single-/multi-fidelity NDTs with fixed fidelity levels cannot adapt to changing network conditions.
AI.method: AdaPTwin employs a hierarchical cloud-edge architecture: the cloud periodically performs computationally intensive fidelity selection, while the edge runs real-time proactive RRM. The edge pipeline includes: (1) trajectory prediction via a transformer model with continual and transfer learning for adaptation to new environments; (2) look-ahead ray tracing using NVIDIA Sionna with a dynamically updated virtual environment; (3) solving a joint RSU beamforming and vehicle-RSU association problem via a scalable multi-start iterative coordinate descent algorithm to maximize proportionally fair sum-rate.
AI.result: Under realistic vehicular conditions, AdaPTwin adapts to diverse scenarios where reactive, single-fidelity, and non-adaptive predictive NDTs fail. It achieves up to 90% sum-rate gain and 80% outage probability reduction compared to non-adaptive NDTs, all while maintaining real-time performance.
AI.conclusion: AdaPTwin successfully demonstrates that dynamic fidelity adaptation based on network conditions is a viable and effective approach for latency-aware, proactive RRM in vehicular networks, significantly outperforming fixed-fidelity alternatives.

title: Engineering Hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Next-Generation Electricity Systems: A State-of-the-Art Review
summary: The integration of machine learning with domain-specific physics is transforming the design, monitoring, and control of electricity systems, where data scarcity, limited interpretability, and the need to enforce physical laws constrain purely data-driven models. Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) addresses these limitations by embedding governing equations directly into the learning process, yielding accurate, efficient, and scalable solutions for Industry 4.0 applications. This article reviews hybrid PIML architectures for electricity systems, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets), Fourier Neural Operators, Extreme Learning Machine-enhanced PINNs, graph-based PINNs (PIGNNs), and domain-decomposition PINNs. Each approach is examined through case studies spanning field analysis, fault detection, digital twins, surrogate modeling, and control optimization. The review shows that embedding Maxwell's equations and other first-principles constraints substantially improves predictive accuracy under sparse and noisy data, reduces simulation time by orders of magnitude relative to finite element methods, and enhances generalization across operating regimes. Hybrid frameworks consistently outperform purely data-driven baselines on parameter sensitivity, dynamic behavior, and robustness, while supporting real-time digital-twin calibration and uncertainty quantification. Persistent challenges include training instability for stiff multi-scale problems, computational cost of high-fidelity models, and the absence of standardized benchmarks. The findings demonstrate that PIML enables a paradigm shift from black-box data-driven methods to transparent, physics-informed strategies, positioning the field for sustained innovation in resilient and intelligent electricity systems.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews physics-informed machine learning (PIML) architectures for electricity systems, including PINNs, DeepONets, Fourier Neural Operators, and graph-based PINNs, demonstrating that embedding physical laws improves accuracy, reduces simulation time, and enhances generalization under sparse data, while noting challenges like training instability and lack of standardized benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Purely data-driven models face limitations in electricity systems due to data scarcity, limited interpretability, and the need to enforce physical laws; PIML addresses these by embedding governing equations into the learning process.
AI.method: The paper reviews hybrid PIML architectures including PINNs, DeepONets, Fourier Neural Operators, Extreme Learning Machine-enhanced PINNs, graph-based PINNs (PIGNNs), and domain-decomposition PINNs, examining each through case studies in field analysis, fault detection, digital twins, surrogate modeling, and control optimization.
AI.result: Embedding Maxwell's equations and first-principles constraints substantially improves predictive accuracy under sparse/noisy data, reduces simulation time by orders of magnitude vs. FEM, and enhances generalization. Hybrid frameworks outperform purely data-driven baselines on parameter sensitivity, dynamic behavior, and robustness.
AI.conclusion: PIML enables a paradigm shift from black-box data-driven methods to transparent, physics-informed strategies for resilient and intelligent electricity systems, though challenges remain in training stability, computational cost, and lack of standardized benchmarks.

title: Bearing-Only Solution to the Fermat-Weber Location Problem for Unicycle Agent
comment: This paper has been accepted for presentation at the 23rd IFAC World Congress
summary: This paper addresses bearing-only algorithms for solving the Fermat-Weber Location Problem (FWLP) with a unicycle agent. Unlike existing FWLP solutions for single- or double-integrator agents, our approach accounts for the nonholonomic constraints of wheeled robots. We first develop a bearing-only control law for the case with stationary beacons. Next, we consider saturated control inputs and propose a corresponding bearing-only control law. Finally, we address moving beacons with constant velocities and develop a control law that enables the unicycle agent to track the moving Fermat-Weber point. Both simulations and experiments are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes bearing-only control laws for unicycle agents to solve the Fermat-Weber Location Problem, considering stationary beacons, saturated inputs, and moving beacons, with validation via simulations and experiments.
AI.motivation: Existing FWLP solutions assume single- or double-integrator dynamics, which do not account for the nonholonomic constraints of wheeled robots (unicycle agents).
AI.method: Three bearing-only control laws are developed: (1) for stationary beacons, (2) with saturated control inputs, and (3) for moving beacons with constant velocities, enabling unicycle agents to track the moving Fermat-Weber point.
AI.result: Both simulations and experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed bearing-only control laws for unicycle agents under various beacon conditions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed bearing-only approach successfully extends FWLP solutions to nonholonomic unicycle agents, handling stationary beacons, input saturation, and moving beacons.

title: Equilibrium-Free Contraction Stability Analysis for Grid-Forming Converter-Based Microgrids
summary: Renewable-driven microgrids dominated by grid-forming (GFM) converters are subject to persistent power fluctuations, making equilibrium-known stability assessments restrictive. This paper develops an equilibrium-free contraction stability method based on semi-contraction theory. By formulating the system in a symmetry-aware projected state space, the intrinsic rotational mode induced by uniform angle shifts is removed. A blockwise Jacobian decomposition is introduced to characterize the coupled active and reactive power dynamics, yielding a computable regional contraction condition. This condition is then converted into forward-invariant stability certificates that provide trajectory-level performance guarantees. For autonomous operation without disturbances, the method provides an equilibrium-free nonlinear stability characterization together with an estimation of the region of attraction (ROA). For non-autonomous operation under disturbances, it derives explicit bounds for quasi-steady tracking under slowly varying injections and for robustness under fast or composite disturbances. Case studies on a 9-bus system validate the proposed method.

AI.tldr: The paper develops an equilibrium-free contraction stability method for renewable-driven microgrids with GFM converters, using semi-contraction theory, symmetry-aware projection, and blockwise Jacobian decomposition to provide trajectory-level stability guarantees under persistent power fluctuations.
AI.motivation: Renewable-driven microgrids with GFM converters face persistent power fluctuations that make traditional equilibrium-known stability assessments restrictive and inadequate.
AI.method: The method uses semi-contraction theory with: (1) a symmetry-aware projected state space to remove intrinsic rotational modes from uniform angle shifts, (2) blockwise Jacobian decomposition to characterize coupled active/reactive power dynamics, yielding a computable regional contraction condition converted into forward-invariant stability certificates.
AI.result: For autonomous operation: equilibrium-free nonlinear stability characterization with ROA estimation. For non-autonomous operation: explicit bounds for quasi-steady tracking under slowly varying injections and robustness under fast/composite disturbances. Validated on a 9-bus system.
AI.conclusion: The proposed contraction-based method provides trajectory-level performance guarantees without requiring equilibrium knowledge, making it suitable for microgrids with persistent renewable-driven fluctuations.

title: Kernel-Based Safe Exploration in Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary:
Safety has been a major concern when deploying deep reinforcement learning algorithms in the real world. A promising direction that ensures that the learned policy does not visit unsafe regions is to learn a \emph{barrier function} along with the policy. A barrier is a function from states to reals that assigns low values to the initial states, high values to the unsafe states, and decreases in expectation on each transition; such a function can be used to bound the probability of reaching unsafe states. Previous attempts learned a barrier function directly from exploration data, but this required either large amounts of data or restrictions on the system dynamics. In this paper, we show how kernel embeddings can be used to learn barrier functions during deep reinforcement learning for stochastic systems with unknown dynamics. Our algorithm, \emph{kernel-based safe exploration (KBSE)}, learns an optimal policy and a barrier simultaneously during exploration. The barriers are computed iteratively, represented as conditional mean embeddings, and provide better probabilistic safety guarantees with more exploration. The exploration algorithm uses the learned barrier functions to identify safety violations. In the case of violation, it intervenes to modify the unsafe action to a safe action, thereby ensuring that the exploration is restricted to actions that bound the probability of reaching unsafe states.
  We evaluate KBSE on several complex continuous control benchmarks. Experimental results establish our new algorithm to be suitable for synthesizing control policies that are probabilistically safe without degradation in reward accumulation.

AI.tldr: KBSE learns barrier functions via kernel embeddings during deep RL to ensure probabilistic safety in stochastic systems with unknown dynamics, intervening on unsafe actions to bound the probability of reaching unsafe states.
AI.motivation: Safety concerns in deploying deep RL in real-world scenarios; existing barrier function learning methods require large data or restrictive dynamics assumptions.
AI.method: KBSE uses kernel embeddings (conditional mean embeddings) to represent and iteratively update barrier functions during exploration; unsafe actions are detected and modified to safe actions based on the learned barrier.
AI.result: KBSE achieves probabilistically safe control policies on complex continuous control benchmarks without sacrificing reward accumulation.
AI.conclusion: Kernel-based barrier learning enables safe deep RL for stochastic systems with unknown dynamics, providing tighter safety guarantees as exploration progresses.

title: Dynamic Lane Allocation in UAM Corridors for Efficient Multimodal Door-to-Door Mobility
summary: This article presents dynamic directional lane allocation in urban air mobility (UAM) corridors as a discrete-time mixed-integer linear program (MILP). This formulation activates, deactivates, and reverses lane direction as bi-directional airspace demand evolves. We model demand from disaggregate ground travel data by decomposing each trip into a multi-modal sequence with first-, middle-, and last-mile legs and routing the UAM-served middle-mile segment through a vertiport-side dispatch model. We use the San Francisco Bay Area as a case study by placing a multi-region spanning corridor between Contra Costa county and Silicon Valley. We find that the dynamic policy cuts unused airspace capacity by 5x, increases mean lane utilization from 36-48% to 67% at the same service level relative to baselines, and reduces commuting-population mean travel time by up to 21.6%. These results show that dynamic configuration of airspace capacity alleviates a significant percentage of the under-utilization issue of lane-based UAM airspace design and UAM concept of operations. This dynamic allocation also provides a safe, structural way to increase throughput, making UAM a more viable complement to multimodal door-to-door mobility systems.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a dynamic directional lane allocation method for UAM corridors formulated as a MILP, which activates, deactivates, and reverses lane direction based on bi-directional demand. Using San Francisco Bay Area case study, results show 5x reduction in unused airspace capacity, increased lane utilization from 36-48% to 67%, and up to 21.6% reduction in mean travel time.
AI.motivation: To address the under-utilization issue in lane-based UAM airspace design where static lane allocation leads to significant inefficiency as bi-directional airspace demand evolves over time.
AI.method: Formulates dynamic directional lane allocation as a discrete-time mixed-integer linear program (MILP). Models demand from disaggregate ground travel data by decomposing trips into multi-modal sequences (first-, middle-, last-mile legs) with vertiport-side dispatch for UAM-served middle-mile segments. Tested on a multi-region corridor between Contra Costa county and Silicon Valley.
AI.result: Dynamic policy cuts unused airspace capacity by 5x, increases mean lane utilization from 36-48% to 67% at the same service level, and reduces commuting-population mean travel time by up to 21.6%.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic configuration of airspace capacity alleviates a significant percentage of lane-based UAM airspace under-utilization and provides a safe, structural way to increase throughput, making UAM a more viable complement to multimodal door-to-door mobility systems.
